_note: The Hole Truth, the colony's monthly newsletter (#424). The sim keeps the month's facts (src/sim/newsletter.ts): keep is how many back issues a hole holds, maxOutcomes how many event outcomes an issue reprints, grumblePoints and praisePoints how many happiness points a cause must cost (or give) before a notable grumbles (or praises) it. The words are src/view/newsletter.ts's: each story is a list of templates, one picked by the issue's dice. Just for fun (`fluff`): the neighbour of the month (a notable the sim picks, `profile`) and, by the dice, fluffPerIssue other sections (fluffQuiet on a quiet month); their placeholders are {name} a made-up colonist and {job} theirs (from `jobs`), {a} and {b} two floors, {x} and {y} a winning and losing score, {w} a small number in words, {crop} (from the section crops list), {spot}. `notices` of the `fillers` go at the bottom. Placeholders: {hole} the hole's name, {n} a count, {w} a count in words, {name} a notable, {role} their job, {trait} one of their traits, {baby} a newborn's first name and {family} a family name (both from data/notables.json), {room} a room's name, {rooms} a list of them, {floor} the deepest floor, {milestone} a milestone's title, {find} what the drill struck (from `finds`, by event id), {pop} the population, {happy} the average happiness. A quiet month reads `rough` instead when health or happiness is below roughBelow. Headlines come from the month's biggest story, in the order of `order`. Voice (docs/ART.md, Voice): warm, dry, a pun allowed, never at the player's expense.
name: The Hole Truth
tagline: All the news that fits the shaft
printed: Physical copies are precious · Please return to the galley when read

head: It's a Martian!
{hole} welcomes its first native
First cry heard below the surface
text: {baby} {family} arrived this month, the first person ever born in {hole}. Both parents report the delivery was 'mostly gravity-assisted.' Children don't work, but they will want a school.
Meet {baby} {family}, {hole}'s first child born on Mars. The clinic staff have already been asked about the view upstairs. A school will be wanted before long.

head: Small arrivals
The nursery fills up
More little Martians
one: Welcome to {baby} {family}, born this month. The clinic reports one tired but very happy family.
{baby} {family} joined us this month, weighing in at about a third of what they'd weigh on Earth.
many: {N} children were born this month, among them {baby} {family}. The clinic asks that everyone please stop asking the newborns about their career plans.
A busy month at the clinic: {w} births, including little {baby} {family}. Lullabies may be heard through the corridors at odd hours.

head: Fresh faces in the corridors
New neighbours
The welcome mat gets dusty
text: {N} new colonists settled in this month. If you see someone staring at the shaft for a long time, they're new. Say hello.
{N} newcomers joined {hole}. They've been shown the galley, the restrooms and which elevator sticks, in that order.
We welcome {w} new neighbours. They report the trip was long, the landing bumpy and the welcome warm.

head: We remember
Fond farewells
text: {N} of our elders passed away this month. They helped dig the place we live in, and they'll be missed.
This month we said goodbye to {w} of our elders. Raise a cup to them at the galley tonight.

head: Grown up and clocking in
Fresh hands on the job
text: {N} of our children came of age this month and joined the workforce. Their first complaint about the shift roster is expected any day now.
{N} young Martians grew up this month. They've never seen a blue sky and they don't seem to mind.

head: Deeper we go
The drill digs in
Floor {floor}, going down
text: The drill finished {w} new floor this month: {hole} now goes down {floor} floors. Elevator music remains under review.
{hole} is now {floor} floors deep. The drill crew would like it noted that they're not boring, they're boring.
many: The drill finished {w} new floors this month: {hole} now goes down {floor} floors. Elevator music remains under review.

head: Ribbon cutting
New doors open
Fresh paint on the rock
one: A new {room} opened its doors this month. Early reviews are positive, if you don't count the smell of fresh sealant.
The crews finished a new {room} this month, on time and only a little dusty.
many: The crews finished {w} rooms this month: {rooms}. Somewhere, a foreman is finally sitting down.
{N} rooms opened this month: {rooms}. The hole is getting roomier, so to speak.

head: The drill strikes {find}
Something down there
A find on floor {floor}
text: The drill struck {find} this month. The crew have filed their report and are already arguing about what to name it.
News from the bottom of the hole: the drill hit {find}. The scientists are thrilled; the drill crew are just glad it wasn't their lunchbox.

head: {milestone}!
A milestone for {hole}
text: {hole} reached a milestone this month: {milestone}. Someone suggested a party. Someone always does.
Mark your calendars: this month {hole} reached {milestone}. The deputy has asked for it to be written down somewhere permanent, so here it is.

head: Party in the hole
A feast below the dust
{hole} celebrates
text: The festival went off with a bang (the good kind). Turnout was excellent and the meals ran out at exactly the right moment.
This month's festival was a hit. Work slowed for a day, smiles didn't. Leftovers are, as ever, a myth.

head: Dust gets in everywhere
Storm passes over
text: A dust storm blew through this month. The solar arrays sulked, the batteries held, and the airlocks are still finding grit.
Weather report: dusty, then dustier, then fine. The storm's gone, but check your boots.

head: A new name to know
text: {name} joined the colony this month and is already making themselves known. Watch this space.

head: A quiet month in {hole}
Nothing to report (and that's good news)
Steady as she digs
text: Nothing much happened this month, which on Mars is exactly what you want. {pop} people, all still breathing.
A quiet month. The air held, the lights stayed on and nobody fell down the shaft. We call that a win.
Slow news month. The editor considered running a story about the new mop in the galley, but decided against it.
rough: Not much news this month, and not much cheer either. People are tired and worried. Better days are a fix or two away; your deputy has notes.
Nothing to celebrate this month. Chins up: the hole has been through worse, and so has Mars.

noise: "I can hear the machinery through my pillow. I'd like a quieter neighbour, or a thicker wall, or both."
smell: "Something smells, and it isn't me. Could someone shut a door between us and wherever that's coming from?"
crowding: "I share my home with more people than I've met. A few more homes, please."
homeless: "Some of us are sleeping in the corridors. It's a lovely corridor. It's not a bed."
airQuality: "The air's stale where I live. I don't need much, just air that hasn't been breathed already."
variety: "Same meal again. I'm not complaining. I'm noting it, for the record, loudly."
noSeat: "There's nowhere to sit at mealtimes. I eat standing up like a horse."
noRestroom: "The nearest restroom is a long walk. A long, urgent walk."
temperature: "Is it me, or is it cold enough down here to keep the milk fresh? I don't have any milk."
noClinic: "If I sprain an ankle, where do I go? Asking for a friend. The friend is my ankle."
schooling: "The kids need a school. I love them, but they've started teaching each other."
elderCare: "Our elders deserve somewhere comfortable to spend their days."
grief: "We have nowhere to lay our dead to rest. It weighs on all of us."
homeWear: "My home's seen better days. So have I, but I can't be repaired by a maintenance crew."
sharedWear: "The common rooms are getting shabby. A bit of upkeep wouldn't go amiss."
holeHealth: "People are feeling poorly. I think it's the water, or the meals, or both. Someone should look."

default: "Things could be better around here. I'm not saying how. I'm saying they could."

windows: "I've got a window on the shaft. I could watch the dust settle all day, and some days I do."
amenityComfort: "The park's lovely this time of year. Every time of year, actually. There aren't seasons down here."
amenityHealth: "Went to the gym. Felt great. Will never shut up about it."
neighbourComfort: "Good neighbours make a good hole. Ours are great."
ownComfort: "I like my home. It's warm, it's mine, and the rock doesn't talk back."
lining: "Whoever finished my walls did a lovely job. I'd tip them if we had money."
sharedLining: "The common rooms look smart these days. Somebody's been busy."
temperature: "Nice and toasty down here. Mars can keep its weather."

finds.ore_vein: a rich vein of iron ore
finds.microfossils: microfossils, the traces of something that lived here once

items: "I told my mum on Earth I live in a hole. She said 'I know, I've seen your room.'"
"If you squint at the shaft lights at night it looks like a city. If you squint harder it looks like a shaft."
"Low gravity's great until you sneeze and end up in the next corridor."
"I've started naming the rocks I dig out. I've stopped telling people that."
"The algae smoothie is better if you don't think about it. Or drink it."
"Does anyone else's airlock sigh when it closes, or is mine just tired?"
"I'm not saying the stew's thick, but my spoon is still standing up in it from Tuesday."
"My plants are doing better than me and frankly they deserve it."
"Someone put a tiny sign on the drill saying 'Hello, my name is Gerald'. It's stuck."
"Sunset's blue here. I've been here two years and it still gets me."
by: a {job} who asked not to be named

items: Low-gravity basketball: the Floor {a} Diggers beat the Floor {b} Drillers {x}–{y}. Three players are still on the ceiling.
The corridor relay was won by Floor {a} for the {w} month running. Floor {b} have lodged a complaint about 'suspiciously good shoes'.
Shaft-ball semi-final: Floor {a} {x}, Floor {b} {y}. The ball has not been recovered.
The monthly slow-walk race was won in a record time of 'eventually'. All entrants were commended for their composure.
Darts night was cancelled after a dart was found to still be in flight. Organisers estimate it will land Thursday.
Floor {a}'s tug-of-war team beat Floor {b} by pulling slightly harder and then everyone falling over very slowly.
Phobos rising: a good month for new beginnings, and for checking your oxygen. Lucky room: the galley.
Deimos in the doorway: someone you've ignored has a good idea. It's probably the drill crew. Listen once.
Olympus ascendant: aim high this month. Not literally; the ceiling's rock.
The Dust Devil: things get stirred up. Keep a broom handy and your opinions to yourself.
Valles Marineris: a long, deep month. Bring a snack.
Earthrise: you'll think of home this month. Write to someone. The delay's only twenty minutes.
A day on Mars (a sol) is 24 hours and 39 minutes. That's 39 extra minutes a day to be late in.
Olympus Mons is about three times the height of Everest, and so wide you couldn't see its top from its edge.
Sunsets on Mars are blue: the fine dust scatters blue light forward, toward the sun.
Mars has two moons, Phobos and Deimos, both about the size of a small city. Phobos is slowly falling toward us. Not this month.
Valles Marineris would stretch across the whole of North America.
Mars has the biggest dust storms in the solar system: some cover the whole planet for weeks.
You'd weigh about 38% of your Earth weight here. Please stop jumping off the gallery to prove it.
Mars is red because of rust: iron oxide in the dust. The whole planet needs a good scrub.
Recipe of the month: {crop} surprise. Take {crop}. Add more {crop}. The surprise is that it's {crop}.
The galley crew's tip: {crop} goes with everything, if you're brave and very hungry.
Chef's special this month is {crop} three ways: boiled, mashed and 'regretfully'.
Try {crop} fritters: a crowd-pleaser, mostly because the crowd has no other options.

Q: My neighbour hums while they work. All day. — Hummed Out, Floor {a}
A: Hum back, a third lower. Harmony is a form of peace.

Q: Is it normal to miss rain? — Dry on Floor {a}
A: Very. Stand under the shower and close your eyes. Don't stay long; it's metered.

Q: Someone keeps eating my labelled yoghurt. — Furious, Floor {a}
A: We don't have yoghurt. Please see the clinic.

Q: How deep will we go? — Curious, Floor {a}
A: Deep enough, and then a little further. The drill decides, mostly.

Q: Can I keep a pet? — Lonely, Floor {a}
A: The algae vats are technically pets. Name one.

traits.Populist: Always on the side of the many, and happy to say so at length.
traits.Cautious: Checks the airlock seals twice and the stew three times.
traits.Industrialist: Believes there's no problem a bigger smelter can't fix.
traits.Idealist: Still thinks we can make Mars kinder than Earth. Might be right.
traits.Greedy: Keeps a careful tally of who owes them a ration. It's a long list.
traits.Charismatic: Can talk a crowd into anything, including double shifts.
traits.Hothead: Has opinions, and they arrive at full volume.
traits.Pragmatist: Prefers what works to what's pretty, and usually gets it.
traits.Earth Loyalist: Keeps Earth time on one watch, just in case.
traits.Martian-born: Never seen a blue sky, and is sick of being asked about it.

outro: Ask them about {spot} sometime; you'll be there a while.
spots: the warm end of the galley
the quiet corner by the scrubbers

fillers: Lost: one left glove, near the airlock. Answers to 'glove'.
Reminder: the shaft is not a rubbish chute. It is a very long way down, and someone has to fetch it.
The galley reports that Tuesday's mystery stew has been solved. It was beans.
Found: one wrench, slightly scorched. Owner may collect from the workshop, and explain.
For trade: one Earth novel, read eleven times. Ending still sad.
Wanted: a name for the drill. 'The Drill' has been ruled out as 'unimaginative' by the drill crew.
Reminder from maintenance: please don't lick the condensation.
This month's sunrise was rated four stars by the people with windows. Everyone else has to take their word for it.
Gravity remains at 38%. Please continue to enjoy it responsibly.
The elevator suggestion box is full. Please stop suggesting stairs.
Reminder: the emergency oxygen masks are not party hats. Even at parties.
Book club this month: the airlock manual. Spoiler: it's about doors.
Free to a good home: one sourdough starter, Earth-born, extremely needy.
The farm would like everyone to stop talking to the potatoes. It's going to their heads.
Choir practice moves to the shaft this month, for the echo. Earplugs are available at the clinic.
Missing: one sock, grey. Last seen entering the laundry. Presumed happy.
The quiet room is for quiet. Whispering 'is this quiet enough?' does not count as quiet.
Lost: a sense of direction, somewhere on floor 2. If found, please point it at the galley.
Night shift reminds day shift that 'good morning' at 03:00 is a matter of opinion.
Movie night: the one about the man stranded on Mars. Again. By popular demand. Again.
Will swap two water rations for one honest opinion of my poetry. No takers last month.
The airlock would like to remind you that it is not a revolving door.
sign: Keep your boots dusted and your hatches shut.
See you next month, same hole, same time.
